dependencies.title: H-Q-4a: sustained gate-failure cancel and sweep
dependencies.description:
`cfg.Params.GateFailDebounce` is configured and tested but has no production
reader. The owner publishes book qualification as telemetry, yet H-Q-4a's
response never occurs: after 30 seconds of a non-qualifying book, adding orders
remain live and fillable while the interval earns no reward.

Implement a per-market, monotonic continuous-failure interval from accepted,
current-generation book state. Before the debounce expires, place no new order
from a non-qualifying book but avoid cancel churn. At expiry, cancel and sweep
every adding order. If q is nonzero, retain or restore only the aggregate-capped
reducer. A fresh complete qualifying book resets the episode; an incomplete,
stale, quarantined, or rejected frame cannot.

Acceptance covers just below/at/above the duration, transient recovery, both
position signs, flat and non-flat markets, existing in-flight/unknown adding
orders, cancel ambiguity, a clock step, disconnect generation changes, and no
resumption from stale truth. Add a composed owner test and a compiling mutation
whose deterministic catcher proves the configured duration reaches its final
consumer.

=== 2026-08-19: OFFLINE REVIEW (no codex). VERDICT REVISE. ONE BLOCKING
=== REGRESSION FOUND AND FIXED; ONE CONFIRMED DEFECT LEFT OPEN.

Codex was out of quota, so the loop's audit/challenge/adjudicate was run offline
with two independent non-codex reviewer threads plus operator adjudication. Note
the independence caveat: both reviewers were Claude-family, so this is
different-model independence, NOT the cross-vendor independence codex supplies.
Every citation below was re-verified by the operator against the source.

The GREEN full gate of iteration 26 was TRUE BUT NOT SUFFICIENT. Seven steps and
287 mutations passed while a blocking regression sat in the change, because no
test covered disconnect-with-inventory or pre-snapshot evaluation, and both new
SETTLING tests inject a clean orders walk BEFORE the replacement leg is sized.
A mutation catalogue can only kill code the tests exercise.

--- D1. BLOCKING REGRESSION. FIXED 2026-08-19. ---

The recap predicate had no target > 0 guard, and target is legitimately 0:

  fundedReducer returns 0 on a nil book OR empty levels (run.go, the levels.Max
  !ok branch). SizesFor sets HasReduce unconditionally for any q != 0 while
  SizeR caps Reduce at funded (skew.go), so wanted stays TRUE and target is 0 --
  the !wanted branch never sees it. The predicate then degenerates to
  atRisk(side) > 0 and cancels ANY resting exit, including a compliant one.

Reachability, traced end to end and then reproduced in a test:
  ApplyDisconnect sets ResetBooks: !clean, so an ABNORMAL close calls
  core.Rig.ResetOnReconnect, which empties every level. The owner loop runs
  evaluate and pump after EVERY select arm including the event arm, so evaluate
  executes immediately with empty books. The recap sits deliberately ABOVE the
  !actionable guard, so its cancel leg dispatches from a book nothing may be
  placed against, and Conditions.Valid then holds the replacement until
  resnapshot. Same collapse at startup with adopted inventory, before the first
  snapshot lands.

Net pre-fix behaviour: on every abnormal disconnect while holding inventory, the
harness DELETED its own correctly-sized exit at the moment it went blind, and
could not replace it until reconnect and resnapshot. That is the exact inversion
of I1 ("no stop path may stop reducing risk") and A4, both of which this unit's
own comments cite. SizeR's doc says an unfundable reducer is "not placed"; the
change silently promoted that to "cancel the one you have".

This was a REGRESSION, not a pre-existing hazard: HEAD has zero
KindCancelConfirmPlace enqueue sites and no cancelConfirmed field at all, so the
entire branch is new. lip-732 also introduces the FIRST activation of the
cancel-confirm-place machinery in quote/queue.go, which was dead code until now.

The in-code comment asserting this "fires on genuine overshoot alone, never on a
compliant exit" was false at target = 0. It has been corrected in place.

FIX APPLIED: guard the predicate on target > 0. Given q != 0, target is 0
exactly when funded is 0 -- either the book is unreadable or capital is
exhausted -- and cancelling the exit is wrong in BOTH cases. Overshoot that
cannot yet be replaced is strictly safer than no exit at all.

TEST ADDED: TestAnAbnormalDisconnectDoesNotCancelTheCompliantExit in
gate_failure_test.go. The exit is sized at EXACTLY the quantized |q|, so the
only thing that can produce a reducing-side cancel is the target collapse; the
clean-close case is the control, and there is a pre-disconnect control assertion
so nothing is attributable to the fixture. Verified to FAIL on both abnormal
cases with the guard reverted and PASS with it restored. build, vet and every
harness package pass with the fix.

--- D2. CONFIRMED, STILL OPEN. Hand to the next round. ---

The replacement leg of the cancel-confirm-place is deterministically unbuildable
in production timing, so the designed confirm-then-place mechanism never
actually operates.

applyWriteResult on Absent calls ConfirmAbsent and sets cancelConfirmed but does
NOT touch pf.LiveOrders. restingOn never consults cancelConfirmed. The same loop
iteration then runs pump: the place leg is released, dequeues, and build calls
targetSize, where remainder = target - atRisk(side) and atRisk still counts the
just-cancelled order. remainder clamps to 0, build errors with "the side is
already carrying its aggregate target", the intents are dropped and a
WRITE_NOT_BUILDABLE SEV2 is raised. Recovery is the fallback path only: the next
complete walk clears LiveOrders and the latch, then decideSide places a fresh
KindPlace.

Cost per recap: one spurious SEV2, and the reducing side ABSENT from the book
for up to position_poll_s rather than the documented single dispatch cycle. The
in-code comment claiming build "sizes the remainder against the shrunken
aggregate" is false at dispatch time.

The two new SETTLING tests structurally step over this window: both inject the
clean walk BEFORE the replacement is sized, then assert the replacement does not
dispatch, and hand-reset the latch. No test in the suite builds the replacement
in the stale-LiveOrders window that production always occupies.

Not fixed here because the repair is a design decision, not a typo: the
defensible fix is to let restingOn discount quantity on a side where
cancelConfirmed is true (ConfirmAbsent is, after all, a complete verifying read
showing absence), but that trades against H-FAIL-3's rule of counting an order
until the exchange confirms it gone. That judgment is worth codex's independent
read rather than an operator's.

MISSING TEST for D2: a production-timing SETTLING case with NO manufactured
post-Absent walk, asserting the place leg acks at 1 contract with zero
WRITE_NOT_BUILDABLE anomalies.

--- D3. NOTED, NOT VERIFIED, LOW WEIGHT. ---

Possible recap churn when a reducer partial fill lands in the orders-then-
positions fetch window: q shrinks before LiveOrders.Remaining does, so atRisk
briefly exceeds target on a healthy at-touch exit. The reviewer conceded the
directive's "possibly-live quantity above target" arguably endorses firing here.
The operator did NOT independently verify the poller ordering claim. Treat as a
churn cost to weigh, not an established defect.

--- ALSO NOTED ---

A composite involving stale Intent.Role on a released StageSecond place leg plus
enqueue deduping on Op() rather than Kind/Role was raised and marked UNVERIFIED
by the reviewer. Both mechanisms are pre-existing and untouched by this diff
(quote/queue.go is not in the deliverable). BUT they are unreachable at HEAD, so
lip-732 is what activates them; it is not a free "pre-existing" pass. Left as a
hunch, not a finding.

dependencies.title: EPIC CR-1: one-market continuous runtime
dependencies.description:
CR-1 means one operator-selected active-program market at S=12 may repeat
maker-entry, reduction, flat and requote cycles without synchronous operator
involvement during one declared market assignment. It runs under launchd and
caffeinate, survives process and websocket restarts through safe adoption, and
either continues safely or durably enters WINDING_DOWN while reduction,
monitoring, heartbeat and alert retry remain alive.

The closed operating envelope is: one selected ticker; dedicated account with
only declared capital and no unrelated cash, positions, orders or manual
activity; manual market replacement; no claim of automatic programme rotation.
Required evidence is a green read-only qualification, clean S=1 first-fill
canary, clean attended S=12 burn-in, final scenario/invariant and operational
readiness, exact full promotion gate, active external dead man, and explicit
operator review.

New work blocks CR-1 only after adjudication that its failure is reachable in
this operating envelope or that CR-1 acceptance cannot be evidenced without it.
Priority labels alone do not move the finish line. Dynamic selection, rotation
and automatic management of unrelated held markets belong to CR-2; CR-1 instead
refuses a dirty account and stops on foreign activity.

Acceptance: record exact commit, config/rung, assignment window, dedicated-
account check, supervision state, runbook/drill evidence and links to all three
promotion rungs. After closure, repeated cycles are authorised only inside that
assignment.

dependencies.title: F8/H-QUE-3: 429 recovery with reserved P1 dispatch
dependencies.description:
Implement F8 for reads, creates, and cancels. A 429 is neither a definite
create rejection nor proof that a cancel failed; preserve ownership and maximum
possibly-live quantity, requeue safely, halve the effective write rate,
exponentially back off with jitter, restore after 60 seconds clean, and emit
SEV2 after 60 seconds sustained.

Backoff must not sleep while owning a dispatcher slot. Reverse the current
one-worker cut: retain one dispatch authority but run a bounded transport pool
with at least one slot reserved for P1 reducers, as H-QUE-3 requires. Keep
capital reservation atomic across workers and prove a hard upper bound from P1
readiness to network dispatch under an unbounded coalesced-cancel storm,
repeated 429s, and one hung non-reserved request.

Acceptance covers 429 on every REST method, Retry-After if present and malformed,
rate halve/restore, jitter bounds, cancellation during backoff, request timeout,
P0/P1 fairness, no duplicate coid, no false cancel absence, and no lost intent.
Add composed scenario coverage and compiling mutations for status
misclassification, immutable rate, sleeping worker, and reducer starvation.

dependencies.title: F5: H-FAIL-6's REST cross-check does not exist, and quarantine strands the reducer
dependencies.description:
Found by the lip-7u4 final-consumer audit. Distinct from lip-2vc, whose
acceptance ("no composed test shows a wedged feed reaching REDUCING") covers the
half that WORKS -- gate.Tick (harness/wsx/gate.go:597-629), called from
cmd/harness/run.go:1191, does reach REDUCING.

THREE FACTS, EACH INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED:

1. H-FAIL-6's cross-check is ABSENT, not deferred behind a stub. F5 requires:
   book silent >60s while socket healthy -> GET /markets/{t}/orderbook, compare
   prices AND SIZES through the full Target Size walk on both sides, including
   our own expected resting size; agree -> reset the staleness clock and KEEP
   QUOTING; disagree -> replace and quarantine.
   There is no REST orderbook fetch anywhere in the tree. Grepping "orderbook"
   across all non-test .go yields exactly one hit, a comment in core/levels.go.
   gate.go:622-624 admits it in its own anomaly text: "H-FAIL-6's full-depth
   comparison is deferred, so this reduces rather than trying to prove the book
   right."

2. THEREFORE F5 IS ONE-WAY. With no cross-check there is no "agree" branch, so a
   quiet market can never resolve back to quoting. It degrades to quarantine +
   REDUCING and stays there.

3. QUARANTINE BLOCKS NEW REDUCER PLACEMENT. cmd/harness/run.go:1300-1316: after
   the cancel branch, "if !actionable { continue }" skips o.decideSide for BOTH
   roles, commented "no PLACEMENT decision may be taken from a quarantined or
   stale book. Cancels are unaffected." Existing resting orders survive and
   cancels still work, which is how §12's "reducing: live" LOOKS satisfied.

THE HAZARD THIS COMPOSES TO, which is why it is P1 and launch-relevant:
a market goes quiet -> quarantined and REDUCING -> resnapshot is LOG-ONLY
(cmd/harness/run.go:757-782 raises RESNAPSHOT_DEFERRED SEV2 and does not
resubscribe; its own comment says the book "stays quarantined until the socket
cycles") -> so if the resting reducer is FILLED, or the position moves so the
reducer needs resizing, NO REPLACEMENT CAN BE PLACED. Inventory then sits
unmanaged until a socket cycle happens for some unrelated reason. A healthy
socket does not cycle merely because one market went silent, so on a one-market
pilot there may be nothing to cycle it.

That is a directional position held open, unattended, with no reducer and no
mechanism to place one. It is exactly the state CR-1 must not be able to reach.

SCOPE -- ADJUDICATED 2026-08-14 BY THE OPERATOR. DO NOT RE-ADJUDICATE.
The earlier (a)/(b)/(c) fork is CLOSED. The driver correctly ruled SPEC_CONFLICT
on it, the operator patched notes/harness-spec.md, and the contract now answers
the question. Implement the spec as it currently reads; see NOTES for the full
decision and the file:line starting points.

In short: new rule H-FAIL-7 retains H-FAIL-6's REST cross-check book as the
reducer's pricing source for the duration of an F5 quarantine, so the reducing
side stays live and resizable while the adding side stays off. A13 is not
weakened -- the quarantined websocket book remains a source for nothing.
H-FAIL-7 also requires an immediate in-session resubscription on disagree, so
the quarantine ends on snapshot + reconcile as F2's does instead of waiting for
a socket cycle that a one-market pilot may never get.

This means (a) and (b) are both IN SCOPE and required, and (c) is superseded by
a narrower, better-sourced rule than the one it proposed.

Blocks the read-only qualification, per lip-7u4's instruction that every
launch-relevant finding must.

=== 2026-08-11, ABSORBS lip-2vc (lip-7u4 final adjudication, codex directive) ===
lip-2vc is closed as superseded by this bead. Its acceptance is NOT dropped --
it is absorbed here, because closing it without carrying the observable forward
would lose the only composed proof required of F5's working half.

WHY SUPERSEDE RATHER THAN KEEP BOTH. This bead's own description says the two
are "distinct", and on the facts they are: lip-2vc was verification debt over a
path that works (gate.Tick, harness/wsx/gate.go:597-629, called from
cmd/harness/run.go:1191, does reach REDUCING), while this bead is a production
defect. But they cannot be SEQUENCED independently. Fixing F5 changes what the
composed path does -- adding the missing cross-check creates an "agree" branch
that lip-2vc's test would then have to account for, and whichever of (a)/(b)/(c)
below is chosen decides whether a quarantined market can place a reducer at all.
A composed test written against today's one-way behaviour would have to be
rewritten by this bead's own fix. Two beads over one seam, where the first must
be redone by the second, is the sequencing this consolidates away.

ABSORBED ACCEPTANCE, carried verbatim in substance from lip-2vc:
  A composed test in cmd/harness -- newRig + serve, not harness/wsx -- in which
  ONE market's book goes silent past the threshold WHILE THE SOCKET STAYS
  HEALTHY, and the harness publishes that market REDUCING with its adding side
  cancelled and swept, A SECOND MARKET UNAFFECTED, and REST and the monitor
  still running.
  The existing detector proof, M-W-QUIET caught by
  TestQuietMarketAloneReducesAndResnapshots, lives in harness/wsx and observes
  the GATE. Per lip-7u4's central finding, a mutation caught by its own
  package's tests proves internals rather than wiring, so the relay mutation for
  this seam needs its catching test in cmd/harness.
  Suspected seam: wsx gate -> PortfolioEffects/Reduce -> owner.noteReduce ->
  quote machine market state.

This bead therefore now carries BOTH obligations: adjudicate and implement the
F5 fix -- (a) implement H-FAIL-6's cross-check, (b) make resnapshot actually
resubscribe, or (c) permit REDUCER placement from a quarantined book while still
forbidding adding, noting (c) alone changes an A13/H-FAIL-4 invariant and must
not be done casually -- AND prove the composed relay above once the chosen
behaviour is settled.

DEPENDENCY NOTE: lip-2vc blocked both lip-q01 and lip-jy4. This bead already
blocked lip-q01; the lip-jy4 link is added in the same change so that closing
lip-2vc removes no gate from the ratchet.
